entries.title: Daemons can now send traces to Vercel Tracing
entries.summary: Vercel Daemons can now send OpenTelemetry traces to Vercel Tracing, allowing you and your agents to inspect background worker operations alongside the rest of your project's traces.Vercel provides each daemon with a Unix socket for receiving OTLP/HTTP traces and sets the socket's path in VERCEL_OTEL_SOCKET_PATH.Upgrading @vercel/otel to version 2.3.0 or later enables automatic trace export for Nod
entries.content:
Vercel Daemons can now send OpenTelemetry traces to Vercel Tracing, allowing you and your agents to inspect background worker operations alongside the rest of your project's traces.

Vercel provides each daemon with a Unix socket for receiving OTLP/HTTP traces and sets the socket's path in 

VERCEL_OTEL_SOCKET_PATH
.

Upgrading @vercel/otel to version 2.3.0 or later enables automatic trace export for Node.js daemons using the default configuration. The SDK detects this socket and sends the spans your worker records to Vercel.

      
import { registerOTel } from '@vercel/otel';
registerOTel({ serviceName: 'my-daemon' });

Initialize OpenTelemetry before the worker starts.

These spans are available through the Vercel CLI, which can search by service name within a project and return JSON for your agents.

      
vercel traces search --project my-project --service my-daemon --json

Search daemon spans from the last hour as JSON.

Learn more in the daemon tracing documentation.

entries.content:
Vercel Token Pass now includes $150 of tokens per month (up from $80) for the same $30 per team per month.

The credit applies to featured open-weight models served through AI Gateway, including Kimi K3, Kimi K3.1 Pro, GLM 5.3, GLM 5.3 Flash, and DeepSeek V4.1 Flash.

Credit resets each billing period with no rollover. When it runs out, requests using standard AI Gateway keys or OIDC tokens fall back to the team's AI Gateway balance, while requests using Token Pass-scoped keys stop with no overage charges.

Token Pass is an Early Access add-on for Pro teams, with limited spots and a waitlist when they fill. To connect your coding agent, run 

vercel token-pass
in the Vercel CLI, or use a Token Pass API key if your agent supports AI Gateway.

Subscribe to Token Pass in your AI Gateway dashboard.

You can limit coverage to selected connected accounts or individual repositories in Agent settings. Once enabled, each push
entries.content:
You can now scan code changes for vulnerabilities with Vercel Security Review in GitHub repositories that have not yet been linked to a Vercel project.

By default, Security Review covers all unlinked repositories the Vercel GitHub App can access in a connected GitHub account. You can limit coverage to selected connected accounts or individual repositories in Agent settings. Once enabled, each push to a covered repository automatically triggers a review of its code changes.

Security Review checks commits directly in repositories with Security Review enabled, without requiring a Vercel project or deployment. When a push creates a deployment for a linked project with Security Review enabled, the review uses the additional project and deployment context.

Connect the account in your team’s Git settings, then enable Security Review in Vercel Agent settings.

Get started with the Security Review documentation.

Contributors

Karen Chen

(iad1) region when reused image data is served from a regional cache.Initialization now reads cached image data close to where the sandbox runs, avoiding round trips to origin image storage in iad1 on cache hits. Regional caching supports managed and custom images backed by Vercel Container Registry, including snapshots ba
entries.content:
Vercel Sandbox now initializes up to 4x faster outside the Washington, D.C. (

iad1
) region when reused image data is served from a regional cache.

Initialization now reads cached image data close to where the sandbox runs, avoiding round trips to origin image storage in 

iad1
on cache hits. Regional caching supports managed and custom images backed by Vercel Container Registry, including snapshots based on those images.

In internal end-to-end benchmarks with Vercel Managed Images, startup time fell about 75% in Paris and from about 3.5s to 1.05s in Seoul. Regions closer to origin storage generally see smaller improvements because requests already travel a shorter distance.

Learn more in the Vercel Sandbox documentation.

Previously, caches were discarded if they exceeded 1.5
entries.content:
The build cache size limit on all Vercel build machines has been increased to 5 GB. This allows projects to save more installed dependencies and framework files for reuse between deployments, which can reduce install and build times.

Build machines are the compute environments that install dependencies and build your project before deployment. Previously, caches were discarded if they exceeded 1.5 GB on Basic and Standard, 3 GB on Enhanced, or 4.75 GB on Turbo, leaving the next build without a cache.

The change applies automatically across all build machine types at no additional charge, with no configuration required.

Learn more in the build cache documentation.

entries.summary: Parallel Decisions Fast from Parallel is now available on AI Gateway and is free through November 23, 2026.It searches the live web to answer typed questions about companies, products, policies, and other changing information, returning probabilities and cited evidence for your application to act on.Use it to enrich CRM records, check eligibility, route leads, or verify claims against current sour
entries.content:
Parallel Decisions Fast from Parallel is now available on AI Gateway and is free through November 23, 2026.

It searches the live web to answer typed questions about companies, products, policies, and other changing information, returning probabilities and cited evidence for your application to act on.

Use it to enrich CRM records, check eligibility, route leads, or verify claims against current sources. Boolean questions return the probability of yes, Choice questions select from options you define, and Score questions assess an ordered rubric. Related questions share context and retrieved evidence in one request.

Use 

parallel/parallel-decisions-fast
as the model name. No separate Parallel account is required. These examples ask the same web-grounded question through the AI SDK, TypeSafe-compatible API, and OpenAI-compatible Decisions API. 
      
import { experimental_decide as decide } from 'ai';
const result = await decide({  model: 'parallel/parallel-decisions-fast',  state: { company: 'Clay', website: 'https://www.clay.com' },  questions: {    has_cli: {      type: 'boolean',      instructions: 'Does this company offer an official command-line interface?',    },  },  providerOptions: { parallel: { includeExcerpts: true } },});
console.log(result.answers.has_cli);console.log(result.providerMetadata?.parallel?.citations);

Citations include source URLs, optional titles, and evidence excerpts. They apply to the whole request, rather than mapping individual sources to each answer. Your application can use answer probabilities to act automatically above a threshold and send uncertain results for review.

AI Gateway tracks these requests in logs and spend budgets alongside other model requests. Read the decision model documentation for question types, or browse the model catalog.

entries.title: Workflow SDK 5: built for production
entries.summary: When we first launched Workflow SDK, the goal was simple: write regular async JavaScript, and let the SDK keep it running through crashes, deployments, and long waits.Last year, we shipped just that, with the world-class developer experience Vercel is known for. Then we watched what our customers built with it.More than 4 billion steps and 700 million runs later, two clear patterns have emerged. T
entries.content:
When we first launched Workflow SDK, the goal was simple: write regular async JavaScript, and let the SDK keep it running through crashes, deployments, and long waits.

      
import { sleep } from "workflow";
export async function welcomeUser(email) {  "use workflow";
  const user = await createUser(email);  await sendWelcomeEmail(user);
  // Survives crashes and deployments  // while it waits  await sleep("3d");  await sendCheckInEmail(user);}

A basic durable workflow

Last year, we shipped just that, with the world-class developer experience Vercel is known for. Then we watched what our customers built with it.

More than 4 billion steps and 700 million runs later, two clear patterns have emerged.

  • The first is automation: Traditional workflows that move data, process orders, coordinate background jobs, manage subscriptions, and run ETL and data pipelines.

  • The second is agents and harnesses: Agents are expensive and long running, so they naturally require durability too.

As those workloads matured, Workflow matured with them. Our priorities have always been security, reliability, and performance.

Here’s how Workflow SDK 5 delivers on all three.

Copy link to headingMore secure workflows

The Workflow event log stores step arguments and return values so a run can recover after a crash or deployment. That data can include sensitive customer information, model context, credentials, and tool-call results. Persisting it requires strong protection.

Workflow SDK encrypts every payload end to end, before it leaves your code. Workflow and step inputs and outputs, hook payloads, and stream data are encrypted with AES-256-GCM, using a unique key for each run. With encryption enabled, any Workflow SDK backend, including Vercel, only sees and stores ciphertext. Plaintext is decrypted in your deployment or in authorized observability tools.

Copy link to headingEncryption with zero configuration on Vercel

On Vercel, encryption needs no setup and no code changes. Each run’s key is derived from a key scoped to the deployment that created it, so a run can only decrypt its own data. Your workflow code doesn’t change:

      
export async function onboardCustomer(  customer: Customer,) {  "use workflow";
  // The customer record is stored  // encrypted in the event log  const account = await createAccount(customer);  await sendWelcomeEmail(account.email);  return account.id;}
async function createAccount(  customer: Customer,) {  "use step";
  // ...and arrives here decrypted,  // inside your deployment  return db.accounts.create(customer);}

Workflow and step payloads are encrypted without changing application logic.

Because Vercel manages the keys by default, observability keeps working. Names, timings, and statuses are always visible, and when you need to see a payload, you can decrypt it in the dashboard or the CLI. Decryption happens in your browser or terminal, follows the same permissions as the project’s environment variables, and every request is recorded in your team’s audit log.

      
# Payloads show as 🔒 Encryptednpx workflow inspect run 
# Decrypts locally, if you have accessnpx workflow inspect run  --decrypt

Inspect encrypted payloads, then decrypt locally with authorized access.

Copy link to headingEncryption on self-hosted Worlds

Encryption is implemented in the SDK, so it can also protect payloads on self-hosted Worlds before they reach storage, queues, or streams.

A custom World enables encryption by implementing 

getEncryptionKeyForRun()
with your key management. Return the same 32-byte key for each run on every call so the SDK can encrypt new payloads and decrypt them during replay: 
      
import type { World } from "@workflow/world";
type RunKeyProvider =  World["getEncryptionKeyForRun"];
export const getEncryptionKeyForRun:  RunKeyProvider = async (run) => {    const runId =      typeof run === "string" ? run : run.runId;
    // Return the same 32 bytes for a run    // every time, so replays can decrypt    return keyStore.getRunKey(runId);  };

Provide a stable 32-byte encryption key for each run in a custom World.

Copy link to headingMore security work in v5

Cross-run writes are sealed too. When code resumes another run’s hook, starts a run in another deployment, or writes into a stream forwarded from another run, the payload is encrypted to the target run’s public key. The writer can encrypt for that run without reading its existing payloads.

You can also limit how long sensitive data is stored. With payload retention set to 

experimental_retention: 0
, inputs, outputs, and stream contents are deleted as soon as a run completes or fails. The run’s metadata stays visible in observability.

Copy link to headingA redesigned trace viewer

The redesigned trace viewer makes runs easier to navigate, with span search, zoom, a minimap, and local inspection during development.

Run attributes are new in v5. They let you attach searchable context to a run, such as an order ID, and then find runs by it. Attributes are plaintext, so they should not contain secrets.

Copy link to headingWorkflows in every region

In Workflow SDK 4, every run lived in 

iad1
. Even when a project was deployed to several regions, each run’s event log, queue, and streams were only stored in one region, so a step running anywhere else made cross-region requests to record its progress.

For v5, we deployed Workflow infrastructure to every Vercel Function region. Each run has its own home region: its state, queue dispatch, and streams are served from the region where it started, without cross-region round trips on the hot path.

By default, a run starts in the region of the function that starts it. Deploy to several regions, and each run stays close to the user who triggered it, with no configuration:

      
import { start } from "workflow/api";import { processOrder } from "@/workflows/process-order";
export async function POST(request: Request) {  const order = await request.json();
  // Runs in the region that served this request  const run = await start(    processOrder,    [order],  );  return Response.json({ runId: run.runId });}

Start each order workflow in the region that handles its request.

To place a run somewhere else, pass a region to 

start()
. That lets a workflow run next to the database it reads and writes, or keep a customer’s data in the region where it has to stay:

      
// Keep this customer’s run data in Frankfurtconst run = await start(  processOrder,  [order],  { region: "fra1" },);

Store this order workflow’s data in Frankfurt.

The 

region
option decides where a run’s data lives. Your steps run where your app is deployed, so deploy to that region too if you want them to execute there. Existing v4 runs stay in 
iad1
.

Copy link to headingInfrastructure reliability

Regional isolation also improves reliability. A disruption in one region does not have to stop new runs in healthy regions. For projects with Vercel Function failover configured, steps can execute in a fallback region while continuing to use the run’s original home region for state. That state remains pinned to its home region; it does not migrate during failover.

With the help of anonymized telemetry and close collaboration with many customers, we found and fixed dozens of rare bugs and race conditions in the Workflow runtime. Workflow SDK also recovers on its own from more kinds of intermittent network errors.

As a result, with Workflow SDK 5, we’ve seen almost no runs fail or stall because of a platform or runtime bug.

Copy link to headingAgent-ready performance

In Workflow SDK 4, every step invocation involved a queue hop to start the step and another to continue the workflow. That is acceptable for slow background automations, but adds latency to the AI workloads developers are building today.

Agent loops and harnesses can contain thousands of sequential events, high-throughput token streams, tool chains, and dynamic subagents. At that scale, the networking and CPU work around every step became a limit.

In Workflow SDK 5, we rewrote large parts of the engine to minimize extra queue hops, unnecessary networking, and CPU work. Across the measured workloads, we saw 1.6× to 25× improvements in measured latency and overhead, while preserving the same developer experience and introducing no major breaking changes.

The benchmarks below compare v5.2.0 with v4.8.12 on Vercel. Pick a measurement to see how v5 compares with v4, then play or scrub through the explainer to see exactly what each benchmark measures.

Workflow SDK 5 includes hundreds of performance improvements to achieve this. Here are some of the major changes behind these numbers:

Fewer queue hops

In v4, each step handed execution back through the queue. In v5, an invocation can execute several steps inline, including parallel steps, before yielding for a wait, a hook, or an approaching timeout.

The runtime also avoids unnecessary persistence round trips and folds step creation into execution. Fewer queue and network requests mean less CPU work and lower runtime overhead. In a five-step benchmark, p75 step-to-step overhead fell from 618 ms to 109 ms.

Incremental replay

Over a 1,020-step benchmark, v4’s p75 overhead grew with the event log: replaying the full event history took time proportional to its size. In the final sampled range, overhead reached 1,748 ms. On v5.2.0, it was 70 ms. The median time to finish all 1,020 steps fell from 21.0 minutes to 3.0 minutes.

WebSocket streaming

Durability should not make a streamed response fall behind its producer. On the Vercel World, v5.2.0 writes streams over WebSockets by default. In a benchmark replaying a 52.4-second agent response, median delivery dropped from 226.1 seconds to 53.5 seconds.

Payload compression reduces the data stored and transferred. AI token streams average around 80% smaller after compression.

These measurements describe one workload, in one region, against the Vercel World. They are a useful view of runtime overhead, rather than a prediction for every application.

Copy link to headingBenchmark results and methodology

Measured October 8, 2026, on Vercel production in 

iad1
, against the managed Vercel World. Each version uses a separate deployment of the same app. Steps take 1 KB of JSON in and out.

Selected results · v4.8.12 compared with v5.2.0

The full results, including tails, are in the performance documentation.

Copy link to headingWorlds: the shared durability primitive

Workflow SDK’s durable functions sit on a World: the interface for storing progress, dispatching work, and delivering streams. That same foundation also now supports fx and durable-harness, which adds durability to existing agent harnesses.

Improvements to the shared storage, queue, and streaming infrastructure can benefit any consumer of a World. Optimizations inside the Workflow replay runtime apply to Workflow SDK; they do not automatically apply to every harness.

Choose the integration around how you want to build:

  • Workflow SDK: write durable application logic with 

    use workflow
    and 
    use step
    .

  • WorkflowAgent: use 

    @ai-sdk/workflow
    for an AI SDK agent loop inside a workflow.

  • fx: embed and extend a native coding agent with libfx.

  • durable-harness: keep an existing supported harness and add durability beneath it.

    • Supports Pi and OpenCode, with experimental integrations for Claude Code and Codex in Vercel Sandbox.

  • eve: build agents with durable sessions powered natively by Workflow SDK and Worlds.

We’ll soon be adding more offerings to our catalog of SDKs and frameworks backed by Worlds for durability.

Copy link to headingBuild with Workflow SDK 5

Besides the improvements above, Workflow SDK 5 also adds:

  • In-flight cancellation with 

    AbortController

  • Searchable run attributes

  • More framework integrations

  • And more

The v5 upgrade docs cover what changed. To start building a new workflow, install the SDK:

      
pnpm add workflow@latest

Install the latest Workflow SDK.

Workflow SDK also has a Python SDK, now in beta, with the same durable workflows, steps, sleeps, and hooks.

Contributors

Alex Langenfeld, Ashwin Venkatesan, Karthik Kalyanaraman, Mitul Shah, Nathan Rajlich, Shalabh Chaturvedi

entries.title: Vercel Sandbox now supports managed npm credentials
entries.summary: Vercel Sandbox can now install your team's private npm packages using credentials stored in team Shared Environment Variables. Custom registries such as GitHub Packages and JFrog Artifactory are also supported.Pass credentials: { npm: true } when creating a sandbox to let it use your team's existing npm credentials.Tokens stay outside the sandbox. The firewall adds authentication to install reques
entries.content:
Vercel Sandbox can now install your team's private npm packages using credentials stored in team Shared Environment Variables. Custom registries such as GitHub Packages and JFrog Artifactory are also supported.

Pass 

credentials: { npm: true }
when creating a sandbox to let it use your team's existing npm credentials.

index.js

      
import { Sandbox } from "@vercel/sandbox";
const sandbox = await Sandbox.create({ credentials: { npm: true } });// Clone or copy project files into the sandbox's working directory first.await sandbox.runCommand("pnpm", ["install"]);

Create a sandbox with managed npm credentials for private package installs.

Tokens stay outside the sandbox. The firewall adds authentication to install requests sent to your configured registries, so a coding agent can install dependencies without seeing the tokens.

Update your Sandbox SDK or CLI to the latest version.

terminal.sh

      
pnpm add @vercel/sandbox@latest

Upgrade the Sandbox SDK or CLI.

Read the npm credentials documentation to get started.

entries.title: Python 3.15 now available as a Vercel Managed Image
entries.summary: Python 3.15 is now available as a Vercel Managed Image for Vercel Sandbox.To run a sandbox with Python 3.15, select vercel/sandbox/python:3.15 using the image option in either SDK or the --image flag in the CLI.The default universal image (vercel/sandbox/universal:latest) still ships Python 3.14 and is scheduled to switch to Python 3.15 on December 16, 2026.Learn more in the Vercel Sandbox images
entries.content:
Python 3.15 is now available as a Vercel Managed Image for Vercel Sandbox.

To run a sandbox with Python 3.15, select 

vercel/sandbox/python:3.15
using the 
image
option in either SDK or the 
--image
flag in the CLI.

sandbox.ts

      
import { Sandbox } from '@vercel/sandbox';
const sandbox = await Sandbox.create({ image: 'vercel/sandbox/python:3.15' });const version = await sandbox.runCommand('python', ['--version']);console.log(`Python version: ${await version.stdout()}`);

Create a sandbox with Python 3.15 and print its version.

The default universal image (

vercel/sandbox/universal:latest
) still ships Python 3.14 and is scheduled to switch to Python 3.15 on December 16, 2026.

Learn more in the Vercel Sandbox images documentation.
